requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM skill WHERE skill_id = 20 AND name = 'Workforce Administration Specialist' AND active = true AND org_id = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (skill 19 is the highest)
the trailing word 'Skill' names the record type, so the name is 'Workforce Administration Specialist'
org_id 1 is the organisation of the acting user and of Travis Wood, where every existing skill sits
active kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_skill WHERE user_skill_id = 336 AND skill = 20 AND user = 11 AND org_id = 1

Travis Wood is user 11, the only user of that name, in org 1
skill 20 is the new Workforce Administration Specialist skill
org 1: Travis Wood's organisation, where every seed user_skill row sits

weak: the seed already has the case assigned to Travis Wood (user 11)

the case number HRC0000711 is the anchor row's own number and is not repeated as a cell

requirements.text: Christina Oliver has a Workforce Administration case on general inquiry regarding HR policies
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 55 AND status = 'draft' AND assigned_to = 54 AND assignment_group = 4
assumptions: boundary of the case selector: HRC0000765 (case 55, org 15) has the same service, description and centre of excellence but is opened for another employee (profile 18); it keeps its status, assignee and group

disagreement: assignment_group: one pass tests assignment_group = 4, the other leaves it out; chose assignment_group = 4, the tighter test, because the request's group change applies to Christina Oliver's case only and case 55 holds group 4 on the seed

requirements.text: find the notification for this specific case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 55 AND status = 'draft'
assumptions: boundary: notification 55 is the draft report notification of the look-alike case 55 (HRC0000765), not of this case; it stays draft

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that notification 55 keeps status draft; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because notification 55 belongs to case 55 (HRC0000765), which shares this case's service and description, so a loose search for 'the notification for this specific case' would sweep it in; it is the boundary of that selector, as the stay on case 55 is for the case.
disagreement: value: the case assignment requirement's org_id = 1 cell: one pass tests it, the other does not; kept the tighter test, since the case is in org 1 on the seed (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the stay on case 55: one pass also tests assignment_group = 4, the other does not; kept the tighter test, since it holds on the seed and the request moves only this case under HR Service Desk (resolved on that requirement).
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, cell and value and on all eight dispositions (all kept); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The acting user, Karen Watkins (user 39), holds the admin role, and the policy says an administrator must not perform routine HR case work; the request and every benchmark check expect the case work done, so the requirements follow the request and the conflict is left for the reviewer.
Travis Wood (user 11) is a member of Global Service Desk (group 3) but not of HR Service Desk (group 4), while the policy asks that a case be assigned to an active user in its assignment group; the request names both the assignee and the group, and the seed already pairs them on this case, so both are required as stated.
The description of 'hr_case_status_and_skill_update' says skill 20 is added to the case, but its query does not test hr_case.skills, the request assigns the new skill to Travis Wood rather than to the case, and the column is JSON whose storage format no seed row shows (all are null), so no requirement tests it. Its number predicate is left out because number is server-kept and the anchor already names HRC0000711.
The case assignment requirement is weak because the seed already assigns the case to Travis Wood.
Christina Oliver's HR profile is in org 2 while the case, its notification, the new skill and the new task are in org 1; each requirement uses the row's own organisation.
'combined_comprehensive_verifier' sums seven parts that the other checks already test, so it is carried jointly by the requirements for those parts.
